newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban authorities inspired by private restaurants.
newsitem.headline: Cuban authorities inspired by private restaurants.

text.p: Authorities in the Cuban capital, apparently inspired by the success of small privately-owned restaurants, have introduced a similar concept of small places to eat, run by the state.

The state news agency AIN quoted local officials in Havana on Wednesday as saying 113 branches of the chain "Ofertas" ("Offers"), have opened to date in the city. The agency said the novelty was that some 17 of them are mini-restaurants, with just four workers and space for 16 customers at a time.

This looks like an imitation of private restaurants, "paladares", that have been allowed in Cuba over the last two years. The paladares function under a plethora of rules including restrictions on what may be sold, a size-limit of 12 chairs and a staff limited to one person and family members only to help.
However, AIN made no reference to paladares in its report on the new state restaurants.

State-run restaurants operating in dollars, for tourists and Cubans with dollars, are often more expensive than paladares. In the peso sector, state restaurants have suffered severely amid economic crisis since 1991, beset by shortages of food and low pay for workers.
